subject: Post-call: ClearWell implementation fit — SDK changes, streaming funcall, and next actions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: ClearWell implementation fit — SDK changes, streaming funcall, and next actions

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking time today. Short recap from our side with clear asks and options so we can align next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- High latency on triage NLP for clinical notes at scale; 95th percentile spikes during batch imports.
- Current reranking pipeline is brittle: embedding index returns noisy candidates requiring manual heuristics.
- Need structured output for clinical extraction (JSON schema) so downstream claims/triage logic can be deterministic.

Goals you outlined:
- Sub-200ms p95 on inference path for triage scoring under steady load.
- 2x improvement in retrieval precision after reranking.
- Deterministic structured output for top-3 extractions to feed internal workflows.

What we proposed on the call (agreement items):
1) Embeddings + reranker: use Redwood embeddings for candidate scoring, followed by a small reranker model (recommended quantized variant) to improve precision.
2) Streaming + function-calls: streaming generation for long clinical context + function-calls for structured extraction into your JSON schema (we'll provide sample mapping).
3) SDK delta: lightweight client hooks to support streaming + a new \"structured_output\" helper on the SDK to validate schemas and surface parse errors. Minimal API surface change — backwards compatible.

Options & engineering estimate (high level):
- Option A (fast path): Embedding + sync rerank, non-streaming, SDK patch (1 engineer, 2 sprints).
- Option B (recommended): Streaming + function-calls + structured-output SDK helper + embedded reranker (2 engineers, 3–4 sprints).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- I will share the integration spreadsheet (attached) with data shapes and example payloads — action: Emily/Mark to confirm schema + retention requirements by EOD Tue 2/16.
- Sergio to schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive focused on streaming/backpressure and reranker latency tradeoffs (target week of 2/22).
- Ben to kick off mutual action plan and include procurement for pricing/contract timing.

Attachments: clearwell-integration-spreadsheet.xlsx (integration matrix), sdk-delta-summary.pdf (high-level SDK changes).

Open questions we flagged on the call (please confirm):
- Data residency / retention policy for intermediate caches — do you need on-prem or VPC-only?
- SLA target: is 99.9% p99 latency required or is p95 the immediate gating metric?
- Any redline constraints from InfoSec re: third-party caching?

If that captures it, I'll convert into a brief MAP (mutual action plan) and send a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Kim

Thanks Kim — this is a helpful recap and captures the main points. A few clarifications from our side:

Priorities for us (ranked):
1) Deterministic structured output to reduce manual triage (most important).
2) Improved rerank precision (second).
3) Latency improvements — we'd accept staged improvements as long as structured output is reliable.

Compliance & retention questions: we must keep PHI in our VPC for at-rest storage; inference can be processed in a private deployment or via secure VPC peering. Can you confirm whether Redwood Private (VPC deployment) supports streaming funcalls today and what the deployment footprint looks like?

Procurement asked for a SOC 2 summary and an expected start timeline for an initial pilot (minimal integration) — I've attached our architecture doc and flagged procurement.

Will review the spreadsheet over the weekend and try to send initial schema confirmations by Tue 2/16 as requested. We are generally inclined toward Option B but need to confirm resource availability.

Subject: Re: Post-call: ClearWell implementation fit — SDK changes, streaming funcall, and next actions

Emily — quick technical notes based on Kim's recap and your questions.

1) Redwood Private & streaming funcalls:
- Yes: our Private deployment supports streaming responses and function-calls. For VPC deployments we run the inference runtime inside the customer's VPC subnet; streaming works over encrypted channels with a small tunnel/proxy component that we validate during onboarding.
- Footprint: a small coordinator VM + 2 inference nodes (NVIDIA A10s recommended) for a pilot that supports ~20–30 qps with streaming. We can size after we see real traffic shapes.

2) Data residency and cache handling:
- We can disable persistent KV cache for the Private deployment if you prefer no intermediate storage. Runtime supports in-memory-only cache per-request.
- Logs: we can route audit logs to your SIEM/S3 bucket; retention configurable.

3) Structured outputs & SDK behavior:
- \"structured_output\" helper will validate model output against your JSON schema and return a deterministic parse error if validation fails. We'll also include an optional auto-repair attempt (1 pass) that can be toggled off.
- Streaming + funcalls will send partial field-level updates (so downstream can start consuming) and emit a final \"commit\" payload once schema validation passes. This reduces tail latency for downstream consumers.

4) Reranker suggestion:
- Recommend a two-stage rerank: candidate embeddings (dense index) -> lightweight reranker model (quantized) executed in the same inference plane to avoid cross-network hops. Expect ~1.3–1.8x cost multiplier over embeddings-only.

Proposed technical next step: 60-minute deep-dive (Sergio + infra engineer + Kimberly) with ClearWell engineering to walk sample payloads and confirm sizing. Available slots: Tue 2/22 10:00–11:00 PST or Wed 2/23 14:00–15:00 PST. Which works for you?
